correctness.rationale: For the fixed alphabet \(\{0,1\}\), each greedy arch is uniquely \(a^r\bar a\) with \(r\ge1\), while the rest is empty or unary. Unique factorization therefore gives \(F(z,u)=(1+z)/(1-z-2uz^2)\). Coefficient extraction proves the exact distribution; cutting after the \(k\)-th arch proves the cumulative count; differentiation proves the moments. The bundled verifier independently checks the defining subsequence property through length \(10\), complete histograms and moments through length \(18\), and the coefficient recurrence through length \(80\). Finite checks are corroboration, not the proof of the infinite statement.
risks: Finite exhaustive checks stop at bounded lengths; the all-length claim therefore depends on the analytic unique-factorization argument and coefficient extraction, which were checked separately.
